question: When two CSS rules tie on specificity, which one actually wins?

beats.speaker: interviewer
beats.line: When two CSS rules tie on specificity, which one actually wins?

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: The two rules carry equal weight, so specificity alone cannot decide between them.
beats.source_quote: Two selectors of equal specificity are tied.

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: The browser falls back to document order, and whichever rule was written last applies.
beats.source_quote: When specificity ties, the rule that appears later in the document wins.

strategy.concept: two rules of equal specificity target the same element
strategy.must_see: two rules side by side, both landing on the same element, neither one heavier than the other

strategy.concept: specificity alone cannot break this tie
strategy.must_see: the scale balanced between the two rules, tipping neither way
strategy.changes_from_previous: the hero moves from neither rule to the tied pair as one unit

strategy.concept: the later rule in the document wins the tie
strategy.must_see: two rules in document order, the later one lit as the winner
strategy.changes_from_previous: the hero moves from the tied pair to the later rule
